category_title: Students with autism exhibiting sensory-maintained skin scratching
minimal_context: Tommy is sitting at his desk in the special education classroom working independently on a packet of math problems.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your math packet for independent work today. Please get started on the first page.

STUDENT: Okay. (Looks at the math packet and begins to scratch his arm)

TUTOR: Keep working on the problems.

STUDENT: This work is challenging. I'm feeling nervous. (Continues to scratch his skin while looking at the packet)

TUTOR: Just try to finish the page.

STUDENT: Scratching feels good and helps calm me down. (Constantly scrapes his own skin with his hand while simultaneously trying to complete the math problems)

options.A: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time with the math packet and feeling nervous.
options.B: Calmly direct the student to avoid scratching and use the stress-relief ball, then withhold attention after this single prompt.
options.C: Provide detailed instruction for each specific element in every math problem in the independent work packet.
options.D: Allow the student to choose between response methods for the math packet (e.g., dictated, oral, written, typed).
